title: Read Shell Midden (15Bt10), Butler County

bodyMarkdown:
On the Green River west of Morgantown, the Read Shell Midden is another Late Archaic camp-and-cemetery in the same mussel-shoal world as Indian Knoll, Carlston Annis, and Ward. WPA crews dug it from 1937 to 1939 under William S. Webb; more than 240 burials were identified, though poor preservation left only about 152 individuals removable for study. Webb’s 1950 report and later paleodemography treat Read as seasonal habitation plus mortuary ground. It joined the National Register in 1986 with the Green River Shell Middens thematic group—Kentucky’s densest Archaic shell-midden landscape, still pinned to the river’s Big Bend.
Source: [https://npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/86000647](https://npgallery.nps.gov/AssetDetail/NRIS/86000647)
